description.value: Steveston Village is a heritage fishing village at the mouth of the Fraser River in Richmond, voted #1 Metro Vancouver neighbourhood out of 192 in 2020 and declared a heritage zone in 1960. It remains a working fishing village where cyclists can buy fresh seafood off the dock, explore national historic sites like the Gulf of Georgia Cannery and Britannia Shipyards, and stroll the waterfront along Fishers Walk. The village's Moncton Street streetscape—lined with cafés, bookshops, and film locations—makes it a compelling stop on any cycling tour of the Lower Mainland.

A human reviewer should confirm whether this node should represent the village as an attraction in its own right or be replaced/supplemented by a more appropriate OSM entity (e.g., a dedicated visitor centre node), and should verify on-the-ground cyclist amenities such as bike racks and washrooms.
enrichment_extras.notes: Steveston Village as a destination is highly relevant to touring cyclists. A site visit or outreach to the Steveston BIA or Tourism Richmond would be needed to confirm bike parking, public washrooms, and other cyclist amenities available within the village.
